references.text: The people repeat their promise of obedience at the covenant ceremony, answering with one voice that they will do all that the Lord has said.
The people reaffirm their commitment to obey the Lord's words after the Book of the Covenant is read to them.
Moses acts as a mediator between God and the people, bringing the people's words back to the Lord.
Israel declares its commitment to follow the Lord's ways and commands in line with the covenant promise.
The people renew their commitment to serve the Lord and obey his voice under Joshua.
Moses' role as mediator between God and humanity points forward to the high priest's service.
Theological contrast: The people's unified obedience (19:8) versus the leaders' challenge to the prophet's authority.
God's direct response to the people's answer from Mount Sinai, confirming that their promise was good.
